machines_on_site.name: AJS 7R special
machines_on_site.text: The first solo hub-steerer, built entirely in-house around an ex-Hailwood AJS 7R engine. Richard raced it at Thruxton and Cadwell Park.
machines_on_site.alt: Richard Difazio at Thruxton in 1968 on the AJS 7R-engined hub-centre special
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: Difazio family archive / The Classic MotorCycle, courtesy of Classic Bike Hub — with thanks.

owners.name: Difazio family / Richard
owners.notes: Raced at Thruxton and Cadwell Park

machines_on_site.notes: First solo hub-steerer; built entirely in-house per TCM.

machines_on_site.name: Triumph Trident
machines_on_site.text: The first hub-steered road bike, seen on Frome’s streets in autumn 1969. Four Tridents were eventually converted.
machines_on_site.notes: First hub-steered road bike; four Tridents eventually converted (CM).

machines_on_site.name: Suzuki 500 “EYB 999J”
machines_on_site.text: Road-tested by several journalists, then sold to a customer in the USA.

owners.name: USA customer (unnamed)
owners.notes: Sold after press tests

machines_on_site.notes: One of the few public registrations known.

machines_on_site.name: BSA Rocket 3
machines_on_site.text: The only Rocket 3 hub-steerer. Kevin sold it in 1977 as a deposit on his first house and bought it back 18 months later.

owners.name: Kevin Charles
owners.notes: Owned since 1975; sold 1977 and bought back; only Rocket 3 hub-steerer

machines_on_site.name: Suzuki GT550
machines_on_site.text: Built from a written-off GT550K, first owned by an RAF fitter, and featured in Bike in 1974. It sold at auction in 2005 for £1,500, with 17,000 miles on it.
machines_on_site.alt: A Suzuki GT550 with a Difazio hub-centre front end
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: BIKE ME!, courtesy of bikeme.tv — with thanks.

owners.name: Roger Margetts (RAF fitter)
owners.notes: First owner

owners.name: Andy Westlake
owners.notes: Bought at auction 2005 for £1,500 / 17k miles

machines_on_site.name: Norton Commando
machines_on_site.text: An Andover Norton press bike converted for Norton’s Mike Jackson. Its owner says the Norton board learned of the project afterwards.
machines_on_site.alt: The hub-steered Norton Commando around 1974–75, soon after conversion
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: Tim (forum member “difazio”), courtesy of Access Norton forum — with thanks.
builders: Difazio (conversion for Mike Jackson / Andover Norton)

machines_on_site.name: Mead & Tomkinson “Nessie”
machines_on_site.text: Difazio supplied Mead & Tomkinson’s first two hub-centre chassis. Their Laverda 1000 racer, with adapted Difazio steering, finished 10th at the 1976 Barcelona 24 Hours.
machines_on_site.alt: The ex-Mead and Tomkinson 1976 Laverda 1000 endurance racer on its Difazio-derived hub-centre front end
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: Bonhams, courtesy of Bonhams lot 417 (2007) — with thanks.

owners.name: Mead & Tomkinson
owners.notes: Ex-works endurance; Bonhams lot 417 (2007)

machines_on_site.notes: ⚠ “Nessie” name applied to Laverda and later Kawasaki machines.

machines_on_site.name: Ducati 750GTE
machines_on_site.text: One of only two complete Difazio motorcycles, with a rare electric-start roundcase engine. It sold at Bonhams for £12,650 in 2019.
machines_on_site.alt: The 1975 Difazio Ducati 750GTE with hub-centre front end
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: Bonhams, courtesy of Bonhams lot 386 (2019) — with thanks.

owners.name: Private (sold Bonhams 2019)
owners.notes: £12,650 on 20 Oct 2019; renovated 1991; Bob Currey prize; 3rd WDW Misano

machines_on_site.notes: ⚠ Bonhams wording “only two complete Difazio motorcycles” is single-source; attribute if restated.

machines_on_site.text: One of two hub-steered Gold Wings, with over 100,000 miles covered. A second hub went on after a crash in 1987.

machines_on_site.name: BMW R65 Difazio Special
machines_on_site.text: The last of five lightweight roadsters built by Richard, this one for himself. Over “twenty five or so years” he built several short-stroke R65 specials, “mostly 94m/m bore 850cc”.
machines_on_site.alt: Richard Difazio’s own BMW R65 Difazio Special, built 2007/8
machines_on_site.credit: Photo: Classic Super Bikes, courtesy of Classic Super Bikes — with thanks.
